evidence.excerpt: Rama said, 'If, O fathers, ye are favourably disposed towards me, the boon I ask is that I may be absolved from the sins born of my having annihilated the Kshatriyas in anger, and that the lakes I have formed may become famous in the world as holy shrines.'
The Rishis said, 'We have a desire to know, O son of Suta, what is implied by the term Akshauhini that hath been used by thee.
Sauti said, 'One chariot, one elephant, five foot-soldiers, and three horses form one Patti;
Time, whose acts are wonderful assembled them on that spot and having made the Kauravas the cause, destroyed them all.
Bhishma acquainted with choice of weapons, fought for ten days. Drona protected the Kaurava Vahinis for five days. Kama the desolator of hostile armies fought for two days; and Salya for half a day.
After that lasted for half a day the encounter with clubs between Duryodhana and Bhima.
At the close of that day, Aswatthaman and Kripa destroyed the army of Yudishthira in the night while sleeping without suspicion of danger.
O Saunaka, this best of narrations called Bharata which has begun to be repeated at thy sacrifice, was formerly repeated at the sacrifice of Janamejaya by an intelligent disciple of Vyasa.
then comes Baka-badha (slaughter of Baka)
The next is called Swayamvara (selection of husband by Panchali), in which Arjuna by the exercise of Kshatriya virtues, won Draupadi for wife.
Maya-darsana (meeting with Maya the Asura architect)
Sisupala-badha (the killing of Sisupala)
the destruction of Sisupala on the occasion of the sacrifice, in connection with offering of arghya
Krimira-badha (destruction of Krimira)
In the last hath been described the battle between Arjuna and Mahadeva in the guise of a hunter.
After this Indra-lokavigamana (the journey to the regions of Indra); then that mine of religion and virtue, the highly pathetic Nalopakhyana (the story of Nala).
After this last, Tirtha-yatra or the pilgrimage of the wise prince of the Kurus, the death of Jatasura, and the battle of the Yakshas.
Markandeya-Samasya (meeting with Markandeya). Then the meeting of Draupadi and Satyabhama
Then the story of Brihadaranyaka and then Aindradrumna.
Jayadratha-bimoksana (the release of Jayadratha).
Then the story of 'Savitri' illustrating the great merit of connubial chastity. After this last, the story of 'Rama'.
then the attempt to take the kine (of Virata by the Kauravas). The next is called the marriage of Abhimanyu with the daughter of Virata.
Sanjaya-yana' (the arrival of Sanjaya). Then comes 'Prajagara' (the sleeplessness of Dhritarashtra owing to his anxiety).
Then 'Yanasaddhi', and then the arrival of Krishna.
Then the story of 'Matali' and then of 'Galava'.
Then the stories of 'Savitri', 'Vamadeva', and 'Vainya'.
Then the story of 'Jamadagnya and Shodasarajika'.
Then the muster of troops and the story of Sheta. Then, must you know, comes the quarrel of the high-souled Karna.
Then comes the arrival of the messenger Uluka which kindled the wrath (of the Pandavas). The next that comes, you must know, is the story of Amba.
Then the death of Abhimanyu; and then the vow of Arjuna (to slay Jayadratha). Then the death of Jayadratha, and then of Ghatotkacha.
Then, must you know, comes the story of the death of Drona of surprising interest.
Then comes the destruction of the Rakshasa Charvaka who had assumed the disguise of a Brahmana (for deceiving Yudhishthira).
Then the coronation of the wise Yudhishthira.
the origin of 'Durvasa', the disputations with Maya.
and the arrival of Narada.
In this last are contained 'Vishnuparva', Vishnu's frolics and feats as a child, the destruction of 'Kansa'
The high-souled Vyasa composed these hundred parvas of which the above is only an abridgement
the son of Suta recited them consecutively in the forest of Naimisha
the destruction of the Asura Vaka
The Paushya parva treats of the greatness of Utanka, and the Pauloma, of the sons of Bhrigu.
The Astika describes the birth of Garuda and of the Nagas (snakes)
the incidents relating to the birth of the celestial steed Uchchaihsrava
the dynasty of Bharata, as described in the Snake-sacrifice of king Janamejaya.
The Sambhava parva narrates the birth of various kings and heroes, and that of the sage, Krishna Dwaipayana
king Bharata--the progenitor of the line that goes by his name--the son born of Sakuntala in the hermitage of the ascetic Kanwa.
the births of the Vasus in the house of Santanu and their ascension to heaven.

In this parva is also narrated the birth of Bhishma uniting in himself portions of the energies of the other Vasus, his renunciation of royalty and adoption of the Brahmacharya mode of life, his adherence to his vows
his protection of Chitrangada, and after the death of Chitrangada, his protection of his younger brother, Vichitravirya, and his placing the latter on the throne
the birth of Dharma among men in consequence of the curse of Animondavya
the births of Dhritarashtra and Pandu through the potency of Vyasa's blessings (?) and also the birth of the Pandavas
Duryodhana to send the sons of Pandu to Varanavata, and the other dark counsels of the sons of Dhritarashtra in regard to the Pandavas
then the advice administered to Yudhishthira on his way by that well-wisher of the Pandavas--Vidura--in the mlechchha language
the burning of Purochana and the sleeping woman of the fowler caste, with her five sons, in the house of lac
the meeting of the Pandavas in the dreadful forest with Hidimba, and the slaying of her brother Hidimba by Bhima of great prowess.
The birth of Ghatotkacha
the meeting of the Pandavas with Vyasa and in accordance with his advice their stay indisguise in the house of a Brahmana in the city of Ekachakra
the extra-ordinary births of Krishna and Dhrishtadyumna
moved equally by the desire of winning the hand of Draupadi on learning the tidings of the Swayamvara from the lips of a Brahmana

In like manner hath the history of Sunda and Upasunda been recited in this.

the escape of the serpent,--and the begetting of a son by that best of Rishis, Mandapala, in the womb of the bird Sarngi.
the description of the lokapalas by Narada well-acquainted with the celestial regions
the destruction of Jarasandha; the deliverance by Vasudeva of the princes confined in the mountain-pass

the fall of Sauva also has been here described by the Rishi
the wailings and lamentations of Yudhishthira on the occasion of his meeting with the worshipful great sage Brihadaswa.
Then Sanatsujata, in which are the mysteries of spiritual philosophy.
Then comes Saraswata, and then the descriptions of holy shrines, and then genealogies.
'Suka-prasna-abhigamana'
Then the arrival of Krishna at the court, and then Bidulaputrasasana.
then comes Baka-badha (slaughter of Baka) and then Chitraratha.

unresolved: Suta in e_suta_address and e_suta_recital may be a parent's designation or a social designation. The separate parent entity and parent claim remain provisional.

The provisional Pandu parent records depend on contextual identification of the named Pandavas with the collectively designated sons of Pandu. The excerpt does not directly state each named individual's parentage.
The provisional Dhritarashtra-to-Duryodhana parent record depends on the phrase connecting Duryodhana's plottings with the other dark counsels of the sons of Dhritarashtra.
The brothers accompanying Yudhishthira in e_yudhishthira_brothers are not individually named there. No named sibling pairs are generated from that collective statement or from shared parent claims.

The continuing possessives in the Bhishma sentence support the Bhishma-Vichitravirya sibling record. The excerpt does not explicitly call Chitrangada and Vichitravirya brothers, so that candidate relationship is omitted.
Draupadi is explicitly Dhritarashtra's daughter-in-law. That affinal relationship has no direct representation among the permitted relationship types.
Draupadi is described as having five husbands, but only Arjuna is individually identified by an explicit marriage claim. No additional husbands are created from the count.

The five sons of the fowler woman, the sons of Bhrigu, the other collectively mentioned sons of Pandu and Dhritarashtra, and Yajnaseni's children are not individually distinguished and are not expanded into separate entities.
The five celestial damsels and five Indras are collectively mentioned without individual identification. No separate entities are created from their counts.

The births of Dhritarashtra and Pandu through Vyasa's blessings, with an explicit question mark, state uncertain birth causation rather than unequivocal parenthood. No Vyasa parent records are asserted.
Births of the Vasus in Santanu's house do not individually establish Santanu as Bhishma's parent.
The births of Ghatotkacha and Vabhruvahana do not identify parents. Arjuna's meeting with Ulupi and carrying away of Subhadra do not independently state marriages.
The unnamed son accompanying Subhadra is not explicitly named Abhimanyu in the transport passage. The two references are kept separate pending an identity statement.
No identity statement equates Kama with Karna, Baka with Vaka, Krimira with Kirmira, or Yudishthira with Yudhishthira. These spellings remain separate.
No identity statement equates Vyasa with Krishna Dwaipayana, Arjuna with Dhananjaya, Bhima with Bhimasena, or Krishna with Madhava or Vasudeva.
The Krishna birth notice and the Krishna of connubial companionship are kept separate from the Krishna identified as a brother. Neither is explicitly equated with Draupadi.
